# Hero Media

> A full-width hero: artwork pinned behind a 16px frame and dimmed, with the content on top.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `media` | slot |  |  |
| `content` | slot |  |  |

## Anatomy

- `root`: The full-width section, 630px tall, on `non-interactive/background/primary`. Its 16px padding is the frame that shows the page around the image. Full width means the container's width, not `100vw`: that includes the scrollbar, and then the sides look about 8px while the top is 16.
- `frame`: The window onto the artwork. It fills the hero inside the 16px frame, with `radius/xlarge` corners, and hides anything that spills out. The rounded `clip-path` is what clips artwork pinned with `background-attachment: fixed`, which `overflow` alone doesn't.
- `media`: The slot for the artwork, filling the frame. The artwork itself is a div with a background image, never an `<img>`: the pinned effect needs a background. Pin it with `background-attachment: fixed` and give it its size in px (the asset's own, e.g. 2336px 1196px), never `cover`: a fixed background sizes itself against the window, not the frame, and blows the artwork up. That bug is why one case study lost the pinned effect the first time. Phones, tablets and reduced motion get `scroll` instead, anchored to the frame.
- `content`: The slot for what sits on top of the artwork. It fills the frame and is never dimmed.

## When to use

- Used at the top of a page that opens with artwork, like a project or an article. One per page.

## When not to use

- A page that opens with words, not an image. The **Paper effect** suits that one better.

## Behaviour

The artwork stays put and the page scrolls over it (`background-attachment: fixed`). Phones, tablets and `prefers-reduced-motion` get a normal static background instead. The dim only works as opacity *and* the colour underneath together. Never change one without the other.

## Accessibility

- **Artwork**: it's a background image, so it's decoration by definition. Anything people need from it goes in the text.
- **Contrast**: check the text against the dimmed artwork, not the colour underneath.
- **Motion**: the pinned effect switches off with `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Where code differs on purpose

| App | What | Why | Taken to design |
|---|---|---|---|
| all | The artwork is dimmed with `opacity/medium` (0.48) on a #171717 frame. Figma's node says 32% (`opacity/mild`). | I set one dim for every case study on 2026-10-18. What you see is opacity times what's underneath, and three heroes looked darker at the same opacity. Figma never caught up. | not yet |
